summary.value: The Red Sex Link, often sold as the Red Star, is a hybrid rather than a true breed. It comes from putting a male of a red breed, usually the Rhode Island Red or the New Hampshire, over a light-colored hen such as a White Rock, Delaware, Rhode Island White or Silver Laced Wyandotte, a cross American hatcheries were using by the 1950s. Several hatchery strains, including the Golden Comet, follow the same idea. Chicks can be sexed by down color at hatch: pullets are red and cockerels pale. Grown hens are red with some white, and roosters are mostly white. Hens weigh about 6 pounds and roosters about 8. A hen lays roughly 240 to 300 large brown eggs a year and rarely goes broody. The birds are friendly and docile and cope with cold and heat. They suit beginners who want a steady supply of eggs.
